title: This Grub Lures Frogs to Eat Them. It Wins Almost Every Time

scenes.text: This frog thinks it's about to eat lunch.
The grub in front of it is an Epomis ground beetle larva, and it's waving its antennae on purpose.
The closer the frog comes, the harder the larva waves. Then the tongue fires.
In a tenth of a second the larva dodges and sinks two double-hooked jaws into the frog's throat.
It drinks the frog's fluids, then chews. In nearly 400 encounters, the frog got the larva into its mouth only seven times.
One toad even swallowed one. Two hours later it threw it up alive, and the larva ate the toad. Lunch is not what the frog thinks.

description:
Epomis ground beetle larvae reverse the food chain: they wave their antennae and jaws to lure frogs and toads, dodge the tongue strike and clamp double-hooked mandibles onto the amphibian, then drain and eat it.
In almost 400 staged encounters at Tel Aviv University, amphibians got a larva into their mouth only seven times, and one toad that swallowed a larva regurgitated it alive two hours later and was eaten by it (Wizen and Gasith, PLoS ONE, 2011).
Which prey animal would you least expect to fight back?
subject: ground beetle larva
first_comment: The adult beetles hunt too: they jump on a frog's back and bite it, and the frog is paralyzed within minutes. Which animal would you never expect to lose to an insect?
